newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: INTERVIEW - Powerscreen says seeks US business.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Powerscreen says seeks US business.

text.p: Northern Ireland's largest publicly quoted company, engineering firm Powerscreen International Plc, said on Tuesday it was actively looking for a new crushing plant in North America.

The group, which reported a 20 percent increase in pre-tax profit to 20.4 million sterling for the six months to September 1996, said its balance sheet was cash positive and its order book for the second half was strong.
"... and there is no reason why this company cannot continue to grow," chief executive Shay McKeown told Reuters.
"We have made about one acquisition per year and ... we are on the lookout to acquire a North American crushing company," he said.
Powerscreen currently has 14 manufacturing locations including Northern Ireland, the Republic of Ireland, Wales, England and North America.

McKeown said the company had also just completed building a factory in Kilbeggan in the Republic of Ireland to manufacture a new range of screening plants for the environmental and recycling industries "which we have to get up and running".

He said the group has worked towards an even spread of its business such that it did not depend on any one country or any one customer. "That is why we have spread our business across continental Europe, the UK, Ireland, North America and Asia-Pacific", he said.
About 34 percent of Powerscreen's sales go to Britian and Ireland, 27 percent to North America, 26 percent to Europe and 13 percent to the Asia-Pacific market.
McKeown said the group's biggest growing market by far was the Asia-Pacific market.
"We are only trading that market (Asia-Pacific) over the last four years and it is a very fast growing market particularly for the screening and crushing division," McKeown said.
Powerscreen said trading for all three of the company's businesses, screening, crushing and materials handling, was well ahead of last year and indications looked positive for the rest of the year.

Group margins, which McKeown estimated at around 14 percent, were broadly maintained in the first half, with an increase in margin in the screening and materials handling divisions offsetting a margin reduction in the crushing and recycling division, it said.
McKeown said as 99 percent of the group's sales were outside Northern Ireland it was not sensitive to political unrest or economic factors within the province.
"Northern Ireland only accounts for one percent of our sales so has no real effect on the company." -- Dublin Newsroom +353 1 676 9775
